name: Aillén mac Midgna

attributes.attribute: a musician of the Tuatha Dé Danann
burned the halls of Tara for twenty-three years
lulled defenders to sleep with fairy music
killed by Fionn Mac Cumhaill with a poisoned spear

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Aillén mac Midgna was the most famous of the Aillén figures. Men called him the burner. He was a destructive musician of the magical tribe called the Tuatha Dé Danann. For twenty-three years in a row he burned down the great halls of Tara. Each year he lulled the defenders to sleep with fairy music so soothing that no one could resist it. After each year's success he crept back to his fairy mound at Finnachaid, and each year Tara was rebuilt. The tragic king Lir was sometimes said to live at that mound as well. The hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill finally killed Aillén with a poisoned spear. The fumes of the spear were so strong that no one could sleep after breathing them, not even those lulled by Aillén's magic.
objective: Record Aillén mac Midgna, the burner of Tara.
key_results: Show his twenty-three-year assault on Tara and his death by Fionn Mac Cumhaill's spear.
